candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record supports AOSD (quotidian fever, salmon-colored rash, arthritis, leukocytosis, markedly elevated ferritin, hepatomegaly) and pericardial inflammation is confirmed on biopsy. However, the benchmark requires 'Catastrophic AOSD with secondary HLH/MAS.' The extremely elevated ferritin (29,161 µg/L), elevated LDH, elevated liver enzymes, and histiocyte-prominent pericardial biopsy collectively point toward MAS/HLH as a distinct and required composite component. C001 captures the parent diagnosis and one anatomic complication but entirely omits the HLH/MAS component and the 'catastrophic' severity designation.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Identifies AOSD with a specific complication (pericardial involvement) but omits the 'catastrophic' qualifier and the critical secondary HLH/MAS component required by the benchmark reference

case_quality_flags: Ferritin of 29,161 µg/L strongly supports MAS/HLH as a required composite component of the benchmark diagnosis
Pericardial biopsy showing histiocytes is consistent with MAS but C001 frames it only as pericardial involvement without MAS context
Absence of hemophagocytosis confirmation on bone marrow biopsy noted; however, clinical and laboratory criteria are sufficient to flag MAS in AOSD context
